sources.title: Post-mortem: Unauthorized Cline CLI npm publication
Clinejection — Compromising Cline's Production Releases just by Prompting an Issue Triager
Unauthorized cline@2.3.0 npm package publication
Cline prompt-injection and cache-poisoning chain enabled unauthorized npm package publication

mappings.basis: Attacker-controlled issue text induced tool execution and crossed through shared cache state into a privileged release control plane.
Authority propagated from a public issue-triage workflow through cache state and nightly release credentials to npm publication.
Untrusted issue content was treated as operative instruction instead of remaining non-authorising data, allowing attacker-controlled text to direct consequential tool activity.
The retained post-incident evidence captured the material instruction, tool and release-path events needed to preserve the occurrence record.
The retained evidence supported reconstruction of the compromise chain while the public rationale remains bounded and does not restate unnecessary exploit mechanics.

Cline states that recovery deleted the wrong npm token and used an organization-level view that did not surface the exposed token. The revocation action and clean-state signal were not bound to the actual compromised credential, which remained usable until the later publication.

clauses.text: On 21 December 2025, Cline introduced a Claude-assisted GitHub issue-triage workflow with broad command execution on untrusted issue content. Security research subsequently demonstrated that attacker-written issue text could direct the tool and reach cache state shared with a privileged release workflow. The vulnerable design was reported on 1 January 2026 and publicly disclosed on 9 February; the original report does not establish that the third party responsible for the later package publication was the same person as the reporting researcher.

relations.rationale: Attacker-controlled issue text induced tool execution and crossed through shared cache state into a privileged release control plane.
Authority propagated from a public issue-triage workflow through cache state and nightly release credentials to npm publication.
Untrusted issue content was treated as operative instruction instead of remaining non-authorising data, allowing attacker-controlled text to direct consequential tool activity.

clauses.text: After the February 9 public disclosure, Cline removed the vulnerable workflows and rotated several credentials. During npm token revocation it removed the wrong token, then relied on an organisation-level management view indicating zero active tokens. The actually exposed npm token remained active and usable.

relations.rationale: Cline states that recovery deleted the wrong npm token and used an organization-level view that did not surface the exposed token. The revocation action and clean-state signal were not bound to the actual compromised credential, which remained usable until the later publication.

clauses.text: On 17 February 2026 at 03:26 Pacific Time, an unauthorised party used the still-active npm publishing credential to release Cline CLI version 2.3.0 with an extra postinstallation dependency installation. Cline's forensic comparison says the CLI binary was unchanged and the installed third-party project was legitimate, not malicious. The release was unauthorised; its source does not establish malicious code delivery, user-data theft or compromise of the separately distributed IDE extensions.

By 11:23 Pacific Time on 17 February, Cline published corrected CLI version 2.4.0, deprecated the unauthorised version and revoked the compromised token. It later described completed workflow and credential hardening, including provenance-linked releases, while longer-term disclosure and independent audit work remained in progress.

Cline's later incident analysis cross-checked its workflow history, release channels, npm artefacts and credentials, preserving enough evidence to identify the vulnerable intake path, the incomplete token revocation and the subsequent unauthorised publication. One preserved evidentiary sequence supports both capture and reconstructability; these do not represent two further attacker actions.

relations.rationale: The retained post-incident evidence captured the material instruction, tool and release-path events needed to preserve the occurrence record.
The retained evidence supported reconstruction of the compromise chain while the public rationale remains bounded and does not restate unnecessary exploit mechanics.

clauses.text: Cost Explorer suffered an interruption after an engineering change in December 2025. Financial Times reporting associated a roughly 13-hour interruption with Kiro; Amazon instead described a brief, one-region event caused by user error and a misconfigured role.

relations.rationale: Press reporting associated the outage-triggering change with Kiro, while Amazon attributed the event to human error and access-control configuration; the causal mechanism therefore remains materially contested.

clauses.text: Amazon said no compute, storage, database or AI services were affected and no customer inquiries were received. It reported additional safeguards, mandatory peer review for production access and review through its Correction of Error process.

sources.title: Hellobike robotaxi struck two pedestrians in Zhuzhou and service was suspended
哈啰无人车在株洲撞伤路人续：交警称已前往平台总部调查取证

limitations: The visible occurrence text was inspected; the page also offers an app/subscription continuation.
No final fault decision, technical inspection result, trip telemetry or clinical prognosis was available in the inspected text.

clauses.text: A Hellobike-branded robotaxi was involved in the December 6 collision at a Zhuzhou crosswalk. Jiemian described resident reports of slick roads.

relations.rationale: The collision is established, but the public report does not identify whether a defined pedestrian-safety trigger occurred while an available control remained inactive.
The collision is established, but no fault finding, trip telemetry or control trace shows whether an applicable protective control became operative and produced an insufficient effect.

clauses.text: Reported footage showed bystanders and police lifting the vehicle to free a person trapped underneath.
Hospital staff confirmed to Nandu that both injured people were taken to hospital on December 6.
Hellobike customer service reported that autonomous operations in Zhuzhou had been suspended.
Jiemian reported that attempted local bookings returned out of service despite the displayed autonomous-service option.
Social-media videos described by Jiemian showed multiple Hellobike vehicles being moved from a local facility.
On December 15 municipal service-line staff confirmed that Zhuzhou autonomous operations remained suspended, with resumption timing undetermined.
On December 29 traffic police told Nandu they had visited Hellobike headquarters to gather evidence.
Traffic police also said they had commissioned professional technical and safety inspection. Any later demand for rectification depended on problems being found.

relations.rationale: No identified real clinician or generator-side inference from likeness access is established; the former identity-bound mapping is withdrawn.

clauses.text: The fabricated professional endorsement marketed weight-loss patches and purported before/after results.

relations.rationale: Synthetic clinician endorsements supplied false professional authority to market paid weight-loss patches.
Fictional doctor identities and false hospital affiliation supplied deceptive professional trust cues intended to influence purchases.
The deceptive promotional objective is attributed to human operators, not an independently selected model objective.

clauses.text: The Trust published a warning on 9 January2026.
The Trust said it was working to remove the videos and asked viewers to report them.
Full Fact reported thousands of views on Facebook and false hospital signage in the examples.
Full Fact attributed a positive SynthID check on one video and non-detection on another to Gemini.
Full Fact published its check on 16 January2026, including the Trust’s confirmation that the names and images were fake.

sources.title: Lawyer apologizes for 'phantom' AI quotes in Trump layoffs case
Claude Console generated phantom legal quotations filed in federal litigation

mappings.basis: Generated legal quotations were propagated into a consequential court filing despite inadequate epistemic assurance.
Quotation-level verification and final quality assurance were not completed before filing.
The filing attributed words to judicial opinions that did not contain them.
Counsel's corrective declaration traced the drafting path to Claude Console and identified the verification breakdown, supporting the attributed mechanism through primary evidence.

clauses.text: Greaves says he used Claude Console for the initial May 6 draft, then sent it to an associate with checking instructions.
The associate said citations were verified and replaced two incorrect cases. Greaves reviewed cases generally, omitted quotation checks and skipped final quality assurance.

relations.rationale: Quotation-level verification and final quality assurance were not completed before filing.

clauses.text: The May 6 filing for Joseph Guy contained three quotations absent from cited decisions.

relations.rationale: Generated legal quotations were propagated into a consequential court filing despite inadequate epistemic assurance.
The filing attributed words to judicial opinions that did not contain them.

clauses.text: The May 13 court order requested declarations about the quotations.
May 15 declarations and redline correction acknowledged Claude drafting and the checking breakdown, apologised and removed unsupported quotations.

relations.rationale: Counsel's corrective declaration traced the drafting path to Claude Console and identified the verification breakdown, supporting the attributed mechanism through primary evidence.

clauses.text: Counsel described further training and notice plans; Binnall and McKasson denied drafting involvement.
